description.en:
Fixture text for Magic Missile: darts of invented light. This paragraph and the ones after it are placeholder prose, long enough that the description has to scroll inside its own area of the lookup.

The second paragraph says nothing about any real rule. It only takes room on the screen, the way a long book entry would, so that the tests can check that nothing is cut and that the text scrolls instead of the whole panel.

A third paragraph follows, with more filler. The darts are made up, their number is made up, and their colour is whatever the reader imagines. None of this comes from a book.

The fourth paragraph continues in the same vein. It mentions a lantern, a ladder and a loaf of bread, because nothing here needs to make sense; it only needs to be long and plain.

A fifth paragraph keeps going. Somewhere a placeholder wizard points a placeholder finger at a placeholder target, and the placeholder darts fly in a straight and very predictable line.

The sixth paragraph is here for height. Long descriptions are common in the real catalogue, and the panel has to handle them at every viewport the layout tests use.

A seventh paragraph, still invented, talks about the weather: mild, with a chance of rain in the afternoon and a light breeze from the west.

The eighth paragraph is nearly the end. The reader who scrolled this far has proved that the area scrolls, which is the whole point of this text.

The last paragraph closes the fixture text: the darts strike one target or several, as desired.

Fixture text for Magic Jar: a soul in a pot. The paragraphs below are invented filler that makes this description long enough to fill the detail panel and scroll inside it.

The pot is plain clay, the lid fits badly and the soul inside complains about the draught. None of this is a rule; it is text that takes room.

A third paragraph adds height. It describes a shelf, a dusty window and a cat that has never once looked at the pot.

A fourth paragraph continues: the caster waits, the clock ticks, and the afternoon goes by without anything happening at all.

A fifth paragraph is still filler. It exists so the layout tests can see the text reach the bottom edge of the panel at every viewport.

The sixth paragraph mentions the weather again, because it is a safe topic: overcast, cool, and quiet.

The seventh and last paragraph ends the fixture text. The pot goes back on the shelf.
